about: The frigate Commonwealth's below-decks stores kit, 1797 (docs/shipkit-stores): the movable things her lower decks fill with, each a mesh in its own frame for the deck slices (the gun deck, the berth deck, the orlop and the hold) to place: mess tables, benches and kids, sea chests, hammocks slung and lashed with their hooks, casks of the navy's sizes with their quoins, shot lockers, the magazine's barrel rack, cartridges, their rack and the passing box. Lengths in feet (_ft) and inches (_in) unless a key says metres (_m) or gallons (_gal). Each value carries its source; 'estimate' means period practice or proportion, not a drawing. stores.py reads this file, build_stores.py builds and checks the kit

sources.falconer_1780: William Falconer, An Universal Dictionary of the Marine (1780 edition, public domain): HAMMOC, 'a piece of hempen cloth, six feet long and three feet wide, gathered or drawn together at the two ends', hung under the deck lengthways, with from 14 to 20 inches allowed between decks for each man's
sources.gun_deck: slice 12 (gundeck_1797.json): the 24-pounder's shot 5.55 in (the garlands), the bore 5.823 in (guns_1797.json); the carronade's bore 6.25 in
sources.casks: the navy's cask sizes as the period's accounts usually give them, in wine gallons of 231 cubic inches: leaguer about 150, butt 108, puncheon 72, hogshead 54, barrel 36; their shapes (length over bilge, head over bilge) are the cooper's usual proportions. Estimate: not checked against a primary list
sources.period: estimate: the period's practice for an American or British frigate of the 1790s where no drawing or dictionary gives the size (the mess tables, forms and kids, the sea chests, the shot lockers, the magazine's racks, the cartridges and the passing box)

frame_note: Every item is built in its own frame: metres, X along its length, Y across, Z up, its origin at the middle of the face it rests on (z 0 on the deck), or for a hung item at the middle between the points it hangs from (z 0 there). build_stores.py writes each item's box, rest, attach points and slots to stores.json; the deck slices turn and place them (linked copies) and check them against the ship with deck.room
materials_note: every material is a name in build_frigate.py's PAINT (Ash, Tin and Fleece come with slice 12): scrubbed deal and ash in Ash, the chests and lockers in Oak, iron in Iron, the powder barrels' hoops in Copper, hammocks and bags in Canvas, bedding and cartridges' flannel in Fleece, line in Hemp, tarred line in Tarred, a hole's dark in Shadow

mess.note: a mess of eight men at a table hung between two guns (the berth deck: between two of its beams' bays): the table's outboard end on a hinge to a cleat on the side, its inboard end hung from the beam over it by two slings, so it hooks up out of the way; a form (bench) either side and the mess's kid, a staved tub with two ears, for its food. Sizes estimate

table.sling_note: sling_to_ft is the default height from the deck to the beam's underside the slings run to (the berth deck's figure is the berth deck slice's: stores.mess_table(sling_m) builds any length)

chest.note: a seaman's chest of pine, painted, its front and back leaning in to a narrower lid (the sailor's chest stands steady in a seaway), the lid with breadboard ends and a skirt, a plinth round the foot, rope beckets through cleats at each end, a hasp and staple. Sizes estimate (period practice)

hammock.note: Falconer's hammock, hempen cloth six feet by three, gathered at each end by its clews (the nettles: small lines from grommets along the end to an iron ring) and hung lengthways from two hooks in the beams by a lanyard at each ring; slung, with its bed in it, and lashed up for stowing in the nettings by day (seven turns of a lashing). Clew length, nettles and the span between hooks are estimate

bed.note: the bed (a flock mattress) and its blanket lying in the cloth

lashed.note: the hammock rolled round its bed and lashed with seven turns of a hammock lashing: the size stowed on end in the nettings (deck_1797.json)

hook.note: an iron hook on a plate screwed to the beam's underside; the lanyard's eye over its bend

hammock.shape_note: slung, the cloth hangs as a trough: each section a circular arc of the cloth's width across a chord (chord_in: at the ends, in the middle), the ends gathered by the nettles (the width drawn in by 'gather' at the very end); its middle sag_in under its ends, the ends drop_in under the hooks. Estimate, by eye from period drawings

casks.note: a staved cask, its staves bellied to the bilge, the heads let in 'chime_in' from each end, iron hoops (copper on the powder barrels, so they cannot strike a spark) at each chime, quarter and bilge, a bung in the bung stave at the bilge. Sizes from each kind's gallons and its length over bilge (L_over_D) and head over bilge (head_over_D): build_stores.py reports the computed gallons beside the card's
casks.hoops_note: each hoop [its middle's place along the length 0..1, at the chimes held in by half its width; its width in inches]

PowderBarrel.use: 100 lb of powder, in the magazine (estimate: its gallons give its size, not a measure)

quoin.note: an oak wedge chocking a cask lying on its bilge, one each side of each end

shot_lockers.note: a bay of the hold's shot lockers: oak posts at the corners, planked ends and back, the front closed by loose boards dropped one above the other into grooves in the posts, filled with round shot; the top layer of shot shows over the boards. Sizes estimate

ShotLocker32.note: the 32-pounder carronades' shot, the bore 6.25 in less its windage (estimate)

magazine.note: the magazine's barrel rack: powder barrels lying on their bilges in two tiers, each barrel in two oak chocks hollowed to it, the chocks on bearers running the rack's length, the upper tier's bearers on uprights; the cartridge rack's shelves of filled flannel cartridges for the 24-pounders, and the passing box a boy carried one cartridge up in. Sizes estimate (period practice)

cartridge.note: a 24-pounder's 8 lb charge in a flannel bag, its end choked (tied) round its neck: the bag a little under the bore (estimate)

budget_tris.note: per unique mesh (they are placed as linked copies: a deck draws each copy, so the meshes copied most, the hammocks and casks, are held lean); the light copy (slice 16) decimates them further. A figure to report against, not a ceiling (Bean, Nov 12: frame rate is the only hard limit): build_stores.py reports each mesh's count against it and never fails on it

meets.note: each item's pieces that meet by design, each [piece, piece, why, the depth in inches either may go into the other (measured, plus a quarter inch, rounded up to a twentieth)]; every other meeting within an item fails the build (deck.room), and so does a pair listed here that no longer meets (a piece that should be let in or rest on another and hangs clear of it). 'items' lists them by item; 'assemblies' by build_stores.py's assemblies, the pieces named '<item>#<copy>.<piece>'
